title: GitHub Actions policy check (.github/policy.rego): verify create-github-app-token scope rule with Conftest by removing one scope input
answers: How do I test that my workflow change passes the GitHub App token scope policy?
How can I confirm a Conftest policy denial fires when owner or repositories is missing?
What is the validation procedure for workflow policy changes in .github/policy.rego?
body:
Path: .github/policy.rego:deny_create_app_token_without_repository_scope is checked by running Conftest over the workflow YAML files in .github/workflows.
Rule: After adding or editing a create-github-app-token step, run Conftest over all workflows, then temporarily delete either the owner or the repositories input from one step and confirm the denial names that job and key; restore the input afterwards. This is how the scope rule was validated for the workflows that set owner: mlflow and repositories: mlflow.
Constraints: Manual check only; no new automated unit test was added for this rule. Run the check on all workflows, not just the edited one, since the rule applies per step across the repo.
applies: Developers changing GitHub App token steps in .github/workflows and validating them against .github/policy.rego.
says: How do I confirm my GitHub App token step change passes the Conftest scope policy?
How can I check that Conftest flags a GitHub App token step missing its owner or repositories input?
What steps should I run to validate a workflow change against the Actions policy before submitting it?
search: Manually validating the GitHub App token scope rule with Conftest: after editing a create-github-app-token step, run Conftest over all workflows, then remove the owner or repositories input from one step to confirm the denial names the job and key. Manual check only; no automated unit test exists for this rule.
